extracted.intended_audience: Members of Parliament and the politically engaged British public concerned with East India Company governance
extracted.subtask_description: A late-18th-century parliamentary speech criticizing the East India Company and ministers' handling of debts, tributes, and appointments relating to Indian provinces (Arcot, Tanjore). It articulates principles of good governance, anti-corruption rules, and standards for adjudication and fiscal policy in colonial administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles to avoid suspicion in pecuniary settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: First, to hear all parties equally, and not the managers for the suspected claimants only; not to proceed in the dark, but to act with as much publicity as possible; not to precipitate decision; to be religious in following the rules prescribed in the commission under which we act; and, lastly, and above all, not to be fond of straining constructions, to force a jurisdiction, and to draw to ourselves the management of a trust in its nature invidious and obnoxious to suspicion, where the plainest letter of the law does not compel it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrounding explanation: if these plain rules are observed no corruption ought to be suspected; if violated suspicion will attach in proportion, and if all violated a corrupt motive must be presumed. (Used as a standard for ministerial conduct in settling Company debts.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy of tribute requires real sovereign protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribute hangs on the sword. It is an incident inseparable from real, sovereign power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to Arcot/Tanjore: imposing a tribute on a prince who is deprived of military power or the right of war/peace is absurd and oppressive; tribute must be accompanied by corresponding protection and sovereign capacity, otherwise it is illegitimate extortion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect essential resources from political extortion
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of the Cavery river (means of subsistence for the people) ought to have no more connection than clouds and rains and sunshine with the politics of the Rajah, the Nabob, or the Company; it should not be contrived as a means of enforcing demands and arrears of tribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance standard: natural resources and means of subsistence must not be conditioned on political arrangements or used as instruments of extortion, since that risks famine and long-term ruin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt fiscal burdens to ability and preserve revenue reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: They do not adapt the burden to the strength, but they estimate the strength of the bearers by the burden they impose. What care is taken to leave a fund sufficient to the future reproduction of the revenues that are to bear all these loads?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiscal-policy criterion: taxes, tributes and subsidies should be set according to the payers' capacity and must preserve a fund to ensure future revenue sustainability; avoid imposing burdens that destroy the taxable base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit oppressive debt terms and compound usury
rubrics_metrics.description: The Company's exactions have loaded countries with a debt generating an usury the most completely ruinous: that is, forty-eight per cent, payable monthly, with compound interest; confiscation of revenues until debt (as the Company chooses to incur) is discharged — effectively forever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial-justice standard: debt arrangements must not impose usurious compound interest or perpetual confiscation of revenues; such terms are inherently oppressive and ruinous and thus unjustifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and consistency in recognizing creditors and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When the outward form of a loan has been renounced or a creditor's name removed from lists, that renunciation should be respected; ministers who provide for the interest of a person on the real but concealed state of his affairs (without regard to ostensible pretences) invite the presumption of confederacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative standard: public officials must be transparent about creditors and transfers, respect prior renunciations or public records, and avoid rewarding concealed interests; failure to do so indicates collusion or corruption (illustrated by the Benfield/Taylor/Majendie/Call transactions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process and appropriate jurisdiction in adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: The way to avoid suspicion is to hear all parties equally and follow the rules prescribed in the commission; it is improper to supersede the decision-making body (the Directors) and to adjudicate without hearing either party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudicative standard: disputes (territorial, pecuniary) should be decided by the proper authority, after hearing all relevant parties and following commission rules; circumventing those procedures breeds suspicion and injustice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using public appointments and honors to reward corrupt financiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Every trust, every honor, every distinction was heaped upon Mr. Atkinson/Benfield: made a Director, made an alderman, (and nearly a representative) to authenticate coalition between men of intrigue in India and ministers in England.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics standard: public offices and honors must not be used as currency to reward or secure the influence of persons implicated in corrupt financial dealings; such patronage demonstrates and entrenches corruption and should be prevented.
